summary: Intake one identified external literature lead as a canonical Library note and exactly one atomic terminal route: existing-node literature anchor, Frontier task, or reasoned rejection. Fully self-contained; executors need no other file.
applies_when: Conservative router: choose this only when the origin issue text unambiguously matches this flow and exactly one flow: it asks to intake ONE identified external literature lead into D5 by creating or reconciling its structured Library note and assigning exactly one terminal disposition (existing-node literature anchor, Frontier task for progress against a specific repository sorry/open obligation, or rejected with a reason). POSITIVE: triage one named paper, DOI, arXiv item, or equivalent source through that three-way disposition. NEGATIVE: do not choose for weekly/cron discovery, broad literature reviews, bibliography maintenance, code features, formalization, or note-only copy edits. OVERLAP: if the issue also requests another independently mergeable deliverable or matches another offered workflow, choose none/plain devloop. AMBIGUOUS: if no single source is identifiable or intake plus three-way triage is not clearly requested, choose none/plain devloop. When uncertain, choose none/plain devloop.

steps.title: Record and route one literature lead

content.generator:
Read the origin issue from its source_ref and emit exactly one child issue title and body for the intake-and-triage step. The child must deliver ONE atomic, independently mergeable PR that records ONE identified external source as a structured Library note and completes exactly ONE terminal route: anchor, task, or rejected. The note and route are one transaction: never create a note in one increment and classify or act on it in another. All rules are embedded below; do NOT consult any external spec file.

SOURCE IDENTITY AND DEDUPLICATION. Verify the bibliographic facts from authoritative source metadata when available; do not invent a title, DOI, claim, license, or locator. Derive the canonical lowercase bibkey as <surname><four-digit-year><first-title-word>, matching `^[a-z]+[0-9]{4}[a-z][a-z0-9]*$`. Before editing, scan every `Library/notes/*.md` note by BOTH exact bibkey and DOI compared case-insensitively. The note address is exactly `D5/L/<bibkey>` and the path is exactly `Library/notes/<bibkey>.md`. If bibkey and DOI identify different existing notes, or the bibkey belongs to a different source, fail closed with no changes and a clear WHY; never add a suffix, alias, duplicate note, or second DOI owner. If this exact source is already fully triaged, do not create another note, anchor, or task; report the existing disposition and produce no changes.

STRUCTURED NOTE. Create or reconcile `Library/notes/<bibkey>.md` as strict UTF-8 without BOM or CR, with canonical YAML front matter containing exactly these seven fields: `bibkey`, `title`, `doi`, `claim`, `strata_touched`, `license`, `triage`. The path and `bibkey` must match byte-for-byte. `doi` is a bare canonical DOI or null, never a resolver URL. `claim` states only what the source supports. `strata_touched` contains only canonical repository GIDs genuinely implicated by the source. Record enough source locator, search evidence, and limitations in the note body to prevent a later rescan. The terminal `triage` value is exactly one of `anchor`, `task(D5/X_Frontier/<Name>)`, or `rejected(<concise non-empty reason>)`; it is never provisional or omitted.

DETERMINISTIC THREE-WAY ROUTE. Evaluate the routes in this precedence order so overlap cannot create two outcomes. (1) TASK wins if the source contains a concrete external result or technique that could discharge or materially attack a specifically identified repository `sorry` or existing open obligation. In the SAME PR, create or update exactly one canonical `D5/X_Frontier/<Name>.lean` task target with a fresh permanent `D5-T####` code when a new task is needed, a task block recording difficulty, dependencies, attempts, actionable hint, and any prior failure evidence, plus a formal open statement when the target requires one. Set the note to `task(D5/X_Frontier/<Name>)`; the GID must resolve, and do not also modify a Blueprint literature reference. (2) ANCHOR applies only when TASK did not: the source directly supports an existing formal declaration or typed Blueprint statement. In the SAME PR, update the canonical Blueprint `*.scribe.cs` definition for the evidenced node, using `LibraryNoteRef.Create("D5/L/<bibkey>")` and `DescribeProvenance.LiteratureAttested(...)`; this derives the ASCII, ordinal, strict-round-trip `lit/<bibkey>` anchor. Emit the deterministic Markdown projection. Keep title and DOI only in the Library note; do not copy bibliographic metadata into the Blueprint. Set the note to `anchor`, and do not create a Frontier task. (3) REJECTED applies only when neither TASK nor ANCHOR applies and the source is affirmatively irrelevant to the repository. Preserve the note and evidence, set `triage` to `rejected(<reason>)`, and make no Blueprint or Frontier change. If evidence is insufficient to distinguish these predicates, fail closed with no changes and a clear WHY rather than guessing or treating ambiguity as rejection.

ATOMICITY, REPLAY, AND VALIDATION. Exactly one note and exactly one disposition may result. Sort any newly added reference collections with ordinal comparison. Re-running against the same source and base must select the same bibkey, path, and disposition and must not append duplicate references, task blocks, or notes. Validate the canonical note parser, DOI uniqueness, all GID round trips and existence checks, typed Scribe construction and byte-identical emissions for ANCHOR, and the Lean/task gates for TASK. Include focused regression coverage when production code changes; TDD/tests live inside this child PR. Do not ask the child to duplicate devloop consensus, CI, PR review, or merge gates; devloop provides those. If no valid atomic change exists, the child must produce NO changes with a clear WHY; no-changes is fatal and blocks the origin.
